steps.question: Which genes have a statistically significant condition-by-time interaction — i.e., a treatment-specific trajectory across t0, t1, t2, t3 beyond the trend shared by both conditions?
acceptance_criteria: Fits a full negative-binomial GLM with design ~ condition + time + condition:time (time treated as a categorical factor with 4 levels, matching the discrete t0..t3 sampling) on the reconciled, filtered count matrix
Fits a reduced model ~ condition + time (dropping the interaction term) and performs a likelihood ratio test (DESeq2 LRT or edgeR glmLRT/glmQLFTest equivalent) comparing full vs reduced
Reports, per gene, LRT statistic, raw p-value, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted q-value for the interaction term

Defines and applies a pre-specified significance threshold (e.g., FDR < 0.05) to call genes with a treatment-specific time trend, and reports the resulting gene count separately from the count of genes significant for the time main effect alone (the shared trend)
Outputs a full results table (gene, LRT stat, p-value, FDR, and per-condition-per-timepoint log2 normalized mean expression) for downstream use

steps.name: Cluster and visualize treatment-specific temporal trajectories
steps.question: Among genes with a significant condition:time interaction, what distinct temporal shapes distinguish the two treatment arms (e.g., early divergence, late divergence, opposite-direction trends)?
acceptance_criteria: Takes the interaction-significant gene set (FDR < 0.05) from T1S2 and computes per-condition, per-time-point mean normalized expression (variance-stabilized or log2 CPM) for each gene

Applies a clustering method (e.g., hierarchical clustering or k-means on standardized trajectories) to group genes by the shape of their treatment-specific divergence over t0-t3, choosing cluster number by a stated criterion (e.g., silhouette score or dendrogram inspection)
Produces trajectory plots (mean +/- SE per condition at each time point) for each cluster, clearly showing where the two conditions' trends diverge
Reports cluster sizes and flags if the interaction gene set is too small (e.g., <10 genes) for meaningful sub-clustering, in which case reports individual gene trajectories instead

steps.question: Are the genes with a significant treatment-specific time-course trajectory enriched for particular biological pathways or gene sets, beyond what shared time-trend genes show?
acceptance_criteria: Runs over-representation or gene set enrichment analysis on the interaction-significant gene list from T1S2 (using human gene symbols already present in counts.csv) against a curated pathway/gene-set collection appropriate for Homo sapiens (e.g., Hallmark, GO, Reactome), if such a reference is available in this environment
Uses the full filtered gene list from T1S1 as the background/universe for over-representation testing, not the whole genome
Reports enriched terms with adjusted p-values (BH-FDR < 0.05) and the leading-edge/overlapping genes per term

If no pathway gene-set reference is available in the environment for Homo sapiens, explicitly reports that enrichment could not be run and returns the ranked interaction gene list as the deliverable instead of fabricating pathway results

plan.title: Treatment-specific time-course DE beyond shared trend
plan.analytical_narrative: Design is 2 conditions x 4 time points (t0-t3), n=3, raw salmon gene counts (12000 genes x 25 samples; metadata has an extra row/column mismatch to reconcile — 24 expected samples vs 25 columns, checked at load). The research question — genes whose change over time differs by treatment, beyond the shared time trend — is a condition:time interaction question in a time-course design, not a simple two-group DE test. The standard rigorous approach is a negative-binomial GLM (DESeq2) with a full model including condition, time (as a categorical factor, since only 4 discrete points are sampled per replicate design) and their interaction, tested against a reduced model dropping the interaction term via a likelihood ratio test (LRT). This isolates genes whose temporal trajectory is treatment-specific from genes that merely respond to time in both arms (the shared trend, captured by the reduced model). Interaction-significant genes are then clustered by their treatment-specific temporal shape and passed to pathway enrichment to characterize what processes diverge over time between conditions. All steps run on the bulk RNA-seq count matrix and its metadata already provided; no external reference beyond generic pathway gene sets is required, and enrichment is planned as an optional enrichment layer that degrades gracefully if no gene-set reference is available in this environment (none is currently provisioned).
